headline_marked: Uber faces [[nearly $1B fine]] in Netherlands over automated driver suspensions
headline: Uber faces nearly $1B fine in Netherlands over automated driver suspensions
summary: Dutch regulators are fining Uber €825 million (approx. $966 million) for deactivating drivers via an automated process without sufficient human oversight.
details: Uber is facing a massive €825 million (around $966 million) fine from the Dutch Data Protection Authority, marking one of the largest penalties issued under Europe's GDPR. The investigation focused on complaints that Uber deactivated driver accounts using an automated system without adequate warning or human review.

The Dutch regulator stated that Uber committed "serious infringements," emphasizing that automated decisions with such significant consequences are unacceptable. This fine stems from complaints that some drivers were permanently deactivated without any human intervention, a point Uber disputes.

Uber has stated it will appeal the decision, arguing that most suspensions are brief, permanent deactivations undergo human review, and drivers have appeal options. The company called the fine "disproportionate."

The case was brought forward by former Uber driver Brahim Ben Ali, who collected testimonies from 170 other drivers and filed a complaint with the Netherlands' data protection authority. He was assisted by PersonalData.io, a digital rights nonprofit.

This is the third fine Uber has received from Dutch regulators, following previous penalties of €290 million for data handling and €10 million for related issues. The digital rights advocate plans to initiate a class-action lawsuit for driver compensation.
